hero.h1: Transcription API for Audio, Video and Links
hero.subtitle: Send a recording or a link to one, get clean text back. TranscriptX handles audio files, video files and public videos from YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and more — with speaker labels, timestamps and over 100 languages.

quickAnswer.question: What is a transcription API?
quickAnswer.answer: It is a service your code calls to turn speech into text. You send audio, video or a media link, and it returns the transcript as data, usually split into timed segments. TranscriptX accepts files and links in the same API and transcribes an hour of audio in about 1–2 minutes.

sections.h2: One API for Files and Links
content: Most speech APIs only take files. If your users paste a YouTube or TikTok link, you end up building a downloader before transcription even starts.
TranscriptX takes either. Upload a file, or pass a URL and the API fetches the media itself. The response looks the same both ways, so you write the handling code once.

specs.label: Input
specs.value: Audio and video files, public video links, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive and direct media URLs

specs.label: Captions needed
specs.value: No — the audio itself is transcribed

specs.label: Speed
specs.value: About 1–2 minutes per hour of audio; tested with 10-hour recordings

specs.label: Accuracy
specs.value: Around 95% on clear audio in our internal tests

specs.label: AI agents
specs.value: MCP server for Claude and other MCP clients

specs.label: Privacy
specs.value: Files deleted after a few days, never used to train AI

items.q: Is a transcription API the same as a speech to text API?
items.a: Mostly, yes — both turn speech into text. For uploading recordings, see the [Speech to Text API](/speech-to-text-api).

items.q: Does it work on videos without captions?
items.a: Yes. The audio is transcribed, so captions are not required.

items.q: Is there a file size limit?
items.a: No. Long recordings do not need to be split first.
